stem: Evaluate the definite integral of (3x^2 - 4x + 1) with respect to x from x = 2 to x = 5.

per_option_rationale.rationale: Taking the antiderivative of -4x as -4x^2 (raising the exponent but not dividing by the new exponent 2): F(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + x. F(5) - F(2) = (125-100+5) - (8-16+2) = 30 - (-6) = 36.
Evaluating the antiderivative only at the upper limit without subtracting the lower limit: F(5) = 5^3 - 2*5^2 + 5 = 125 - 50 + 5 = 80.
Building the correct antiderivative F(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x but adding F(2) to F(5) instead of subtracting: 80 + 2 = 82.

explanation: Find the antiderivative term by term: integral of 3x^2 is x^3, integral of -4x is -2x^2, integral of 1 is x. So F(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 + x. Evaluate: F(5) = 125 - 50 + 5 = 80 and F(2) = 8 - 8 + 2 = 2. The definite integral = F(5) - F(2) = 80 - 2 = 78.

explanation_sections.punchline: The setup decision is correctly building the antiderivative term by term and then subtracting (not adding) the lower-limit evaluation.
explanation_sections.approach: Multi-term polynomial integration: integrate each term using the power rule (raise exponent by 1, divide by new exponent), then apply the Fundamental Theorem: integral = F(upper) - F(lower).
explanation_sections.lesson: After raising the exponent by one you must also divide by the new exponent. Skipping that division is the most frequent power-rule error in integration.
explanation_sections.timing: 60-80 seconds. Opt 3 (80) signals the student stopped after evaluating at x=5; opt 4 (82) signals an addition sign instead of subtraction.
